verdict.rationale: Floot documents an official remote MCP server that external agents (Cursor, VS Code, Zed, Claude, ChatGPT) can connect to. Through it they can build endpoints, tables and screens, read logs, run SQL and create checkpoints, using the user's own AI subscription rather than Floot credits, so an outside agent can drive the builder instead of the built-in one. The evidence does not show that the external agent can work alongside the built-in assistant on the same project, and nothing beyond vendor claims confirms it. missing for 10: documented co-existence/hand-off between an external agent and the built-in assistant, full enumeration of code/UI-editing tools available over MCP, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect my own coding agent to the project so it drives the builder alongside or instead of the built-in one

citations.quote: Add Floot to Cursor, VS Code, Zed, or any client that supports remote MCP servers
It runs on your existing Claude or ChatGPT subscription over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), not Floot credits.
It lets you build and ship full-stack apps without leaving your AI chat — works with Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and more
Describe the integration you want to your AI assistant, and the endpoints, database tables, and screens get built for you.
